# Satoshi's coins are not lost. They are pending.

> 21/Aug/2026: Crypto stands on the brink of its first post-quantum bailout. Build the exit before the emergency.

This epigraph is intentionally rhetorical. It is a warning about migration timelines, not a claim that cryptographically relevant quantum computers can take coins today. The benchmark makes the underlying engineering question concrete: if large reversible ECDSA arithmetic becomes practical, how efficiently can the required circuit be expressed, and how much time will classical-signature ecosystems have left to migrate?

Shoutout to the QRL Community and to [@moscowchill on X](https://x.com/moscowchill) for supporting this run and keeping the post-quantum migration question visible. The best bailout is the one built, tested, and adopted before anybody needs it.

## What was merged

The latest promoted frontier changed only the 48-bit identity-tail nonce. Its arithmetic body remained the Q1279 interleaved construction from the preceding submissions. This branch formally merges that promoted commit, then adds the exact dead-low arithmetic reduction from the earlier R700 work to the current architecture.

The dead-low idea and its earlier validation were documented in the Kimi-assisted `8910bd1` submission. That contribution deserves explicit credit. The work here was to recover the non-overlapping reduction after later structural submissions replaced that source area, port it onto the Q1279 schedule, recheck every call-site invariant against the current implementation, merge the newest public frontier, find a fresh valid tail stream, and certify the result through the unchanged challenge harness.

The resulting editable changes remain limited to:

- `src/point_add/arith/const_arith.rs`, which adds exact dead-low controlled constant-add and constant-subtract helpers;
- `src/point_add/pingpong_div.rs`, which selects those helpers only at call sites with a structural proof;

No evaluator, simulator, serializer, score writer, build script, dependency manifest, or benchmark harness is changed.

## Exact low carry and borrow elimination

The controlled constant arithmetic uses a ripple state. For addition, the first carry is determined by the accumulator bit, constant bit, and control. For subtraction, the first borrow uses the complemented accumulator bit. In simplified Boolean form:

```text
carry_0  = acc_0 AND constant_0 AND control
borrow_0 = NOT(acc_0) AND constant_0 AND control
```

If constant bit zero is clear, the first state is structurally zero. A call site can also prove the first state is zero from a relation among its live operands. Once the incoming carry or borrow is zero, each following zero bit in the constant extends the zero run. The omitted ancillas would remain `|0>` for every computational-basis input, and every omitted gate would map zero to zero. This is an exact circuit reduction, with no statistical assumption and no added approximation probability.

The new helpers calculate that dead prefix, allocate ripple ancillas only from the first position that can become live, and preserve the existing majority, sum, measurement, and phase-repair sequence above it. If a call site supplies no proof and the constant does not establish a dead first position, the helper falls back to the original full ripple.

## Call-site proofs

The secp256k1 pseudo-Mersenne correction is `f = 2^32 + 977`. Its low bit is one and bits 1 through 3 are zero. The five migrated call-site families have direct invariants.

### Conditional modular negation

The negation correction subtracts `f - 1`. Because `f - 1` has bits 0 through 3 clear, the first four borrow positions are structurally zero from the constant alone. No operand correlation is required.

### Modular halving

The halving cell copies `target[0]` into the control qubit named `parity`. For subtraction by odd `f`, the first borrow is:

```text
NOT(target[0]) AND parity
= NOT(target[0]) AND target[0]
= 0
```

The zero bits 1 through 3 of `f` extend that exact dead-borrow prefix.

### Modular doubling

The doubling cell shifts the target before applying the correction. That shift leaves `target[0] = |0>`, so the first controlled-add carry is zero for every control value. Again, zero bits 1 through 3 of `f` extend the dead prefix.

### Round-one seed and inverse seed

The seed correction uses `f - 1`, whose clear low bits establish the dead run structurally. The forward seed selects the subtraction helper and the inverse seed selects the addition helper, preserving their previous inverse relationship.

These proofs concern only the low ripple state. The Q1279 walk/replay interleaving, R700 depth, terminal passenger loans, endpoint window, coefficient registers, chunk boundaries, square, and reverse multiplication schedule remain unchanged.

## Frontier merge and nonce qualification

During this work the public board advanced from commit `ffc4e07` to `11f5d9a`. A direct source comparison showed one changed editable line: the default terminal nonce moved from `320000001` to `104000102`. There was no new arithmetic or qubit-lifetime change to stack.

The final Git history still merges `11f5d9a` explicitly. The merge conflict was the nonce literal alone. Its frontier value cannot certify a changed operation body because the Fiat-Shamir hash, test inputs, and measurement stream all move when structural operations are removed. A fresh search for the combined stream selected nonce `320004246`.

`apply_tail_nonce` changes the targets of 48 cancelling X/X pairs at the end of the circuit. Each pair remains an identity, so the logical point-add map is unchanged. The encoding changes the Fiat-Shamir seed used by the canonical challenge evaluator. The winning nonce was accepted only after all 141 batches, covering all 9,024 shots, completed with clean classical outputs, phase, and ancillas.
